sections.overview: The carpet chameleon is native to Madagascar; its historical wide-ranging species concept was revised when southern and northwestern populations were separated as other species.
sections.identification: Adults reach 17–25 cm; males are often green with a pale flank stripe, while heavier females are more colorful.
sections.habitat: It inhabits trees and shrubs in humid, partly shaded areas, including gardens.
sections.diet: It catches flies, grasshoppers, crickets and larvae among foliage.
sections.behavior: Diurnal, it basks before hunting among vegetation.
sections.reproduction: Females bury eggs in soil; clutches contain 8–23 eggs, with up to three yearly.
sections.ecology: Its range and taxonomic limits need care: the former southern form is now Furcifer major, and the northwestern form is F. viridis.
sections.conservation: IUCN assessed it as Least Concern with a stable trend in 2014, but that assessment predates taxonomic revision and is marked as needing an update.
